 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P (MV) No.993 of 2003 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thalassery.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the appellant/claimant, on 16.02.2003 at about 2.45 p.m., while the petitioner was travelling in a jeep bearing registration No. KL-7-S-7146, driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, along with his family members, the vehicle overturned, resulting in serious injuries to the claimant.
The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 3,00,000/-.
3. The 1st respondent/driver and 2nd respondent/owner of the offending vehicle remained ex parte before the tribunal.

The 3rd respondent/insurer of the offending vehicle, contended in its written statement that it is not liable to pay compensation since the insured had violated the permit conditions by carrying more passengers than permitted.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A33 and Exts.B1 to B3 and Ext.X1 were marked and PWs 1 and 2 were examined.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a MACA NO. 2602 OF 2014 2025:KER:83442 sum of 2,38,800/- as compensation under different heads with interest @7.5%
per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs against the 3rd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurance company.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads :-
Notional income :-

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 4,000/- was claimed, the tribunal had taken only an amount of 3,000/-
as the monthly income of the injured who was a rubber tapper.

The learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that, as per the judgment in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the income of a coolie for an accident in the year 2003 is fixed at 4,000/- per month and sought for enhancement of fixation of monthly income.

sentences.text:
Following the MACA NO.
2602 OF 2014 2025:KER:83442 judgment in Ramachandrappa (supra), in order to award a just compensation, I find it is appropriate to refix the monthly income as 4,000/-.
Loss of earnings :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tribunal has taken only a period of five months for awarding compensation under the said head and sought enhancement of compensation.

The petitioner had sustained following injuries :-

sentences.text: Considering the nature of injuries sustained as well as age of the appellant, I am inclined to take a period of eight months for awarding compensation under the afore head.
Since the monthly income is refixed at 4,000/-, the total compensation payable under the head loss of earnings, is recalculated thus: 32,000/- (4,000x8).

The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 15,000/-
towards MACA NO. 2602 OF 2014 2025:KER:83442 loss of earnings.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 17,000/- under the head loss of earnings.
Pain and sufferings :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 15,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained as well as the age of the appellant, I find that a total amount of 20,000/- can be awarded under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 5,000/- under the afore head.
Loss of amenities :
- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tribunal has not granted any compensation towards loss of amenities.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained and loss of enjoyment in life, I find that a total amount of 20,000/- can be awarded under the said head.

Permanent Disability :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal, by taking into consideration the principles under the Workmen's Compensation Act, fixed the permanent disability of the petitioner at 30%.

It is further submitted that, apart from the loss of one eye, the appellant also suffered paralysis and had difficulty in sitting, as stated in Ext.A17 disability MACA NO. 2602 OF 2014 2025:KER:83442 certificate issued by the doctor who treated him and assessed his permanent disability at 35%.

On the other hand, the learned standing counsel for the insurance company submitted that, as per the Workmen's Compensation Act, the disability for the loss of one eye is assessed at 30% and hence, the tribunal has correctly adopted the same.

On a perusal of Ext.A17 disability certificate, it is seen that the doctor had stated as follows :-
"paralysis of left side of face, partial weakness of right side of body, no vision in left eye, Aphasia - difficulty in speech due to paralysis of tongue and painful movement of back and left (injured) leg.
Considering the afore facts, I find that the functional disability of the appellant can be fixed at 35%.

Since the monthly income has been refixed as 4,000/-, following the judgments in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)] and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)], is recalculated as: 2,68,800/- (4,000x12x16x35/100).

Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.
Since the appeal is of the year 2014, I find it appropriate to fix the interest @7% per annum on the enhanced amount.

7. Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:-
Sl.

Medical expenses 75,000 32,000 (not modified) 32,000 5 Pain and suffering 15,000 5,000 20,000  1,65,000 6 Permanent 1,72,800 96,000 2,68,800  disability 7 Loss of amenities - 20,000 20,000

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the claimants are awarded an additional amount of 1,38,000/- (Rupees one lakh thirty eight thousand only) over and above the compensation awarded by the tribunal with interest @7% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs from the 3 rd respondent.
The respondent insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimants shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the respondent insurer to make the deposit as ordered above.
